guard_3.verdict: the code was correct; the guard's oracle was wrong
guard_3.why_it_failed: It asserted document.body.innerText contained the contiguous string "21%". valHTML puts the number in a <b> and the unit in an <i>, so the laid-out copy yields "21\n%" and that substring never exists. The two percentages that DO appear as text, 80% and 62%, are the warn threshold and a deliberate counterfactual explaining the exclusion.
guard_3.now_asserts: dataFill=21 · geometry=21% · valueText=21% · billed=21% · valuation=62% · cost identity holds
guard_3.second_error_found: The first replacement measured the FIRST matching .u11w-mrow. This widget renders into three panes (overview, costs, analytics) and only one is laid out, so that read a hidden copy with a zero-width track. The guard now filters to the visible copy.

guard_4.verdict: the guard was right to fail, but for a different reason than it reported, and it was too weak to say so
guard_4.what_its_six_hits_actually_were: The lineage block's labelled identity row. Its regex required see|ref|event before the id and \s+ spans newlines, so "This event" + newline + "ue-615" matched. Those hits were not the defect.

deliberately_kept.what: An internal id that is the entire text of its own element, or the value of a labelled key/value row.
examples: the ledger's id column, which sits beside an 'inspect' button
'Follows / user work · ue-501' as a labelled kv value
deliberately_kept.why: These are identity displays on Advanced detail surfaces, not prose. The audit finding was about a dead end inside a sentence; an event ledger showing event ids is the conventional and useful thing, and removing them would leave a reader nothing to quote back. The exemption is implemented structurally - the id must be the whole text of its element, or a labelled sibling must name it - so it cannot quietly widen to excuse whatever the code happens to do.
deliberately_kept.disclosed_as: a scoping decision, not a closure
